learn.title: Read what the compiler says
learn.body: Compiler messages look scary but follow a pattern: `file:line:column: kind: text`. They tell you where to look and often what is wrong. Read the first one before anything else.

learn.title: Warnings are not optional
learn.body: An error stops the build. A warning lets it finish, but it flags code that is probably wrong. Treat every warning as a bug to fix. The flags `-Wall -Wextra` switch on many useful ones.

learn.title: Two warnings
learn.body: It builds, with two warnings: `n` is never used, and `%d` expects an int but got 2.5. Running it prints junk, which is undefined behavior.

learn.title: An uninitialized variable
learn.body: `x` was never given a value, and the compiler warns when it is read. The output is unpredictable, so give every variable a value.

learn.title: Take a message apart
steps: `warning` means the build finished but something looks wrong
The text after it says what and why

learn.body: Add `-Werror` to turn every warning into an error, so none slips by.

questions.explanation: The order is file, line, column.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between an error and a warning?
choices: An error only appears at link time
An error stops the build, a warning does not
questions.explanation: A warning still deserves a fix, because the code is probably wrong.

questions.prompt: Which flag turns every warning into an error? Type it.
questions.explanation: `-Werror` makes a warning fail the build.
These flags make the compiler point out suspicious code.

questions.prompt: The compiler warns that `x` is uninitialized. What should you do?
choices: Give `x` a value before reading it
questions.explanation: An uninitialized local holds an unpredictable value, never a safe 0.

questions.prompt: You see five errors. Which do you fix first?
questions.explanation: Later errors often come from the first. Fix it and rebuild.

questions.prompt: Match each part of a message to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Messages are consistent, so learn the pattern once.
